content: Ultimately, while the broader analyzed sources heavily focus on general toll systems, technological advancements, and national tariff adjustments, they frequently omit explicit descriptions of the localized toll operators active in Mpumalanga and Limpopo [3] . SANRAL and TRAC are inferred to play foundational roles in the overarching toll management architecture across South Africa, providing the infrastructure upon which these regional operators function. However, the absence of updated and specific insights into local corporate operators in public archives underscores a noticeable gap in available information related to the specific timeframe of the query. The lack of directly relevant findings in contemporary public sources makes it challenging to definitively map the entire operational scope of all minor processing entities in these provinces as of June 2026 [1][3] . As of June 2026, the sector demonstrates a profound commitment to innovation, operational efficiency, and ecological sustainability, particularly through the utilization of Dense Medium Separation and jigging technologies. These methodologies remain foundational to the mineral processing sector, providing robust solutions for gravity-based mineral separation. Appropriate Process Technologies, headquartered in Johannesburg, serves as a prominent provider of these small to medium-scale mineral processing solutions . Their specialized engineering in Dense Medium Separation and jigging systems is essential for the beneficiation of high-value commodities widely mined across South Africa, most notably chrome and manganese . By focusing on tailored engineering, firms like Appropriate Process Technologies align with the growing regional demand for adaptable and highly efficient processing solutions, sustaining a strong manufacturing and operational presence within the country [14] . The official platforms of such enterprises further outline their deep specialization in Dense Medium Separation and jig technologies for various minerals, underscoring their critical relevance to the South African mining and toll processing ecosystems [15] . In parallel with Dense Medium Separation, jigging technology represents a major pillar of the competitor landscape in South African toll processing. Foundational principles of hydraulic jig technology rely heavily on density segregation for effective ore beneficiation, a method that has been continuously refined over the past decade [13] .
